security_audit.summary: Audit found expected outbound HTTP behavior in scripts/ensembl_query.py and SKILL.md examples for the public Ensembl REST API. Markdown code fences produced many external-command false positives; only the documented package installation commands require manual caution. No prompt injection or hidden exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Outbound Ensembl queries may include sensitive genomic identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy notice and tell users not to send restricted or identifiable data without approval.

remediation.issue: Installation examples fetch Python packages with uv pip install.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dependency installation user-approved and pin trusted package names or versions where practical.

remediation.issue: Network destinations are spread across examples and scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Document allowed domains, including rest.ensembl.org and grch37.rest.ensembl.org, in one security note.

content.value_statement: Genomic research often needs fast access to genes, variants, sequences, and assemblies. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Ensembl REST workflows.
actual_capabilities: Look up genes by symbol or Ensembl identifier.
Retrieve genomic, transcript, and protein sequences from Ensembl.
Query variants and Variant Effect Predictor results.
Find orthologs, paralogs, and comparative genomics data.
Map genomic coordinates between supported assemblies.
Use a bundled Python helper script with rate limiting and retries.
limitations: Requires network access to public Ensembl REST endpoints.
Results depend on Ensembl availability, release data, and rate limits.
Does not replace clinical interpretation or validated diagnostic workflows.
Sensitive human genomic queries need separate privacy review.

use_cases.title: Annotate a Gene List
use_cases.description: Convert gene symbols into Ensembl identifiers, coordinates, transcripts, and cross references for a research table.

use_cases.title: Review Variant Consequences
use_cases.description: Check variant records and VEP predictions before preparing a research summary or internal report.

use_cases.title: Compare Genes Across Species
use_cases.description: Find orthologs and assembly details for comparative genomics projects across model organisms.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up One Gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Ensembl database skill to look up BRCA2 in human. Summarize the Ensembl ID, location, transcripts, and key cross references.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Sequence retrieval for a known identifier.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ensembl to retrieve the genomic sequence for ENSG00000139618. Return a concise summary and note the response format used.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Variant Effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Query Ensembl for rs699 in human and summarize population data, known consequences, and any VEP-related interpretation boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Comparative Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Ensembl workflow for comparing human BRCA2 orthologs in mouse and zebrafish. Include endpoints, rate-limit handling, and output fields.

output_examples.output: A gene summary with the Ensembl identifier, chromosome location, strand, transcript count, and relevant database cross references.

output_examples.input: Find orthologs for a human Ensembl gene ID in mouse.
output_examples.output: A comparison summary listing matching orthologs, species names, confidence notes, and fields useful for downstream analysis.
A variant summary covering location, alleles, population frequency availability, and caution notes for interpretation.

best_practices: Confirm species names and genome assemblies before running queries.
Use batch endpoints and caching for large gene or variant lists.
Respect Ensembl rate limits and retry only after the advised delay.
anti_patterns: Do not submit sensitive or identifiable genomic data without approval.
Do not treat Ensembl responses as clinical diagnoses.
Do not run large repeated queries without batching, caching, or rate limiting.

faq.question: What data source does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the public Ensembl REST API and bundled endpoint documentation.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: No API key is shown in the skill. Anonymous Ensembl access is rate limited.

faq.question: Can it retrieve DNA or protein sequences?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers genomic, transcript, and protein sequence retrieval.

faq.question: Can it analyze variants?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports variant lookup and Variant Effect Predictor workflows through Ensembl endpoints.

faq.question: Is it suitable for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. Use validated clinical systems and qualified review for diagnostic or treatment decisions.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
